findings.title: Expand home paths before passing them to the Python smoke runner
findings.trigger: An executor follows the changed activation plan to construct or rerun run_smoke.py.
findings.execution_path: Task 3 supplies cwd `~/triggarr` and a tilde-prefixed --add-dir value to a Python subprocess argument-list invocation. Python does not perform shell tilde expansion.
findings.consequence: The positive activation smoke test fails before Claude starts because cwd is interpreted as a literal relative directory. The generated driver paths also fail the plan's stated absolute-path requirement.
findings.evidence: The diff replaces the previous absolute paths with ~/ paths. A read-only reproduction using subprocess.run(..., cwd="~/triggarr") raised FileNotFoundError. The general pytest evidence does not exercise these agent-instruction snippets.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep paths portable by explicitly constructing them with Path.home() or Path(...).expanduser(), then pass the expanded strings as cwd, --add-dir, and paths embedded in the smoke driver.

limitations: Pytest was not rerun independently because the sandbox is read-only; exact-head harness evidence was inspected instead.
The publication-gate self-test creates temporary repositories and was not executed under the read-only restriction. Its implementation and both scripts' syntax were inspected.
Live GitHub configuration and external tool behavior were not queried; review was restricted to files inside this working copy.
The reproduced finding verifies Python path handling, not a complete live activation run.
Large initial tool outputs were truncated; targeted reads and programmatic comparisons were used to cover the omitted in-scope changes.
